rule.calendar_observation: every pull's answer for every leader is appended once to calendar_facts.jsonl (append-only) with the row's OWN pulled_utc as observed_utc, its pull_id and source. A report date d acts on the decision at time T only while the newest observation with observed_utc <= T names d (as next_date or last_reported_date); FAILED rows and rows naming no date carry no information and are skipped. So a date announced ahead acts on time; a date first observed after its reaction session's close is LEARNED_LATE and acts only on decisions after its observation (never retroactively; stored rows never change); a date replaced before its reaction close is MOVED and never acts
rule.calendar_stale_rule: at the run: the forward calendar is STALE when its newest FULL_UNIVERSE receipt is older than calendar_stale_days, not OK, or its snapshot is damaged (forward_calendar.freshness), or a leader's own row is CALENDAR_STALE / NOT_COVERED / served from an older snapshot, or a leader has no bars; a step then exits 3 naming it. A leader whose fresh row holds no next date is UNSCHEDULED: named (OVERDUE when its last report is older than unscheduled_overdue_days), exit 0. A next date beyond calendar_horizon_days is SCHEDULED_FAR: healthy
rule.definition: at the close of a leader's earnings-reaction session s with open_s / close_(s-1) - 1 <= gap_threshold, stock exposure = gross_after_event for sessions s+1 .. s+sessions_after_event (overlapping events: the minimum)
rule.earnings_dates: forward_calendar/snapshots/fc_<stamp>_<h6>.jsonl (task AegisForwardCalendar, forward_calendar.py): per pull and leader the vendor's next_date, timing, event_utc, event_time_known, confirmation, last_reported_date. The v1/v2 past-report cache straddle_forward/earnings_cache.json is not read
rule.gap: open_s / close_(s-1) - 1 of the leader on the reaction session s, from the bars
rule.non_earnings_gaps: do not fire (as the replay code ran; NVDA 11-09 / 11-12 2026 excluded)
rule.reaction_session: the first session whose OPEN is strictly after the report time. The report time is the newest pre-event observation's event_utc when the calendar states the time (event_time_known: BMO -> the report date's own session, AMC or intraday -> the next session); when the time is not stated (timing UNKNOWN, or a VENDOR_ESTIMATE) it is the CLOSE of the report date, so the reaction session is the next session: the convention that cannot read a price before it existed. A date first named only after its event takes its time from that first observation (last_reported_utc when stated, else the close of the date). One reaction session per report (v2 checked two)

rule.book_returns_for_beta: sessions <= D: the entry weights held at constant weight (backcast, cash at 0); sessions >= E: the book's realised NAV return, paired with QQQ over the same interval (E: open to close)
rule.definition: if close_(t-1)(QQQ) < SMA_sma_sessions(QQQ closes through t-1): short QQQ over session t with notional h x NAV, h = min(beta_(t-1) clipped to beta_clip, hedge_notional_cap, gross_cap - stock exposure x gross long); beta_(t-1) = OLS beta of the book's daily returns on QQQ's over the beta_window sessions ending t-1; otherwise no hedge
rule.gross_cap_why: the brain's decision of 2026-11-15: a book named preservation may not exceed 2.0x gross. v2 admitted 3.95x (beta clip 3) and held 2.49-2.90x in the backfilled window. The cap binds at every decision (each close, after the rebalance); between closes the legs drift with prices (a +10% QQQ session at the cap moves gross to ~2.28x before the next close rebalances it)
